text:
Sam: Heads up — p99 tail spiked on the canary this morning around 14:20 UTC, looks like a combo of kernel selection + KV-cache behavior.
Maria: ugh, any link to the run? which model and microbatch config?
Sam: canary id 2026-03-18-14, model=rw-large, microbatch=8, kernel=auto, kv_cache=enabled. Load test had a bunch of long-context chats (~2k tokens).
Raj: auto kernel switch landed in last rollout (kernel-selector v2). It prefers flash_attn for medium seq, but we saw regressions on long sequences in the CI perf matrix.
Noah: grabbing the profiler dump now, will post a quick snippet.
Noah: ```
# top events (nvprof simplified)
flash_attn_forward   avg 2.2ms   p99 7.8ms
flash_attn_backward  avg 3.1ms   p99 12.2ms
gemm_optim           avg 0.9ms   p99 1.2ms
KV_lookup            avg 0.5ms   p99 4.6ms (miss amplification)
GPU_util             avg 82%    p99 98%
```
Lina: KV hit rate drop from 88% -> 45% during the spike? That will amplify tail (more full-attn work).
Sam: exact numbers: before spike kv_hit=0.87, during=0.46. Also microbatching increased queueing for long requests.
Maria: so two amplifiers: 1) kernel choice increased per-token cost for long seq; 2) lower kv hit -> more compute; 3) microbatching increased head-of-line blocking.
Raj: possible mitigations: pin kernel for long-seq models (force_gemm for seq>1024), reduce microbatch to 4 for canary, or raise admission headroom target from 80% -> 70% util.
Noah: quick experiment results: reducing microbatch=4 reduced p99 by ~35% but throughput down ~18%. For canary that p99 improvement got us back under SLO.
Lina: sounds inline with theory. We should also consider prefetched KV warmups for chat starters to avoid cold-miss storm.
Maria: is there a low-effort admission control we can toggle? maybe an aggressive queue-depth limit or request-size cutoff?
Sam: DeployBot can flip admission gamma, but need clear guardrails. Current admission aims at 85% GPU util during normal load. I propose temp drop to 75% for canary rollout.
Raj: also want a narrow kernel patch: kernel-selector should check seq_len histogram and prefer gemm path for seq>1024. I'll open a PR with heuristic + perf tests.
Noah: created short follow-up load test: 1) microbatch=8 kernel=auto (bad), 2) microbatch=4 kernel=auto, 3) microbatch=8 kernel=force_gemm. Results: case 2 and 3 hit p99 SLO but case 1 fails.
Lina: do we have a simple circuit-breaker to shed very long requests when GPU queue > threshold? that would limit tail risk.
Sam: we have admission-shed but it's coarse (percent-based). We can add size-based shedding quickly.
Maria: action items:
- Raj: PR kernel-selector heuristic for seq>1024 (due EOD)
- Noah: run full canary matrix with microbatch=4 + size-shed toggle (start now)
- Lina: sketch KV prefetch warmup plan and metric dashboard for kv_hit by origin
- Sam: flip admission target to 75% for canary and monitor p95/p99
DeployBot: note: changed admission_target util to 75% for canary (temporary). :white_check_mark:
Raj: fyi I'm adding a perf regression test to CI that simulates KV-miss storms + long contexts so we catch this earlier.
Sam: thanks all — let's try the two-pronged approach: kernel heuristic + temporary lower util. If that gets stable we can iterate on batching heuristics and KV warming. :thumbsup:
Maria: one more thing — add an alert for sudden kv_hit drop >20% in 5m window; that would have caught this earlier.
Lina: agree, adding alert + dashboard card.
Noah: posting logs + flamegraphs to the canary thread, will link in the ticket.
Sam: linking ticket #INF-2247 with the dump and the canary links.
Maria: good postmortem candidate if we don't fully close this in the next canary. keep updates here.
